Pro.16.4.bsb: The LORD has made everything for His purpose—even the wicked for the day of disaster.
Pro.16.4.kjv: The Lord hath made all things for himself: yea, even the wicked for the day of evil.

Pro.26.10.bsb: Like an archer who wounds at random is he who hires a fool or passerby.
Pro.26.10.kjv: The great God that formed all things both rewardeth the fool, and rewardeth transgressors.

Pro.20.9.bsb: Who can say, “I have kept my heart pure; I am cleansed from my sin”?
Pro.20.9.kjv: Who can say, I have made my heart clean, I am pure from my sin?

Pro.3.35.bsb: The wise will inherit honor, but fools are held up to shame.
Pro.3.35.kjv: The wise shall inherit glory: but shame shall be the promotion of fools.

Pro.16.31.bsb: Gray hair is a crown of glory; it is attained along the path of righteousness.
Pro.16.31.kjv: The hoary head is a crown of glory, if it be found in the way of righteousness.

Pro.10.6.bsb: Blessings are on the head of the righteous, but the mouth of the wicked conceals violence.
Pro.10.6.kjv: Blessings are upon the head of the just: but violence covereth the mouth of the wicked.

Pro.5.19.bsb: A loving doe, a graceful fawn—may her breasts satisfy you always; may you be captivated by her love forever.
Pro.5.19.kjv: Let her be as the loving hind and pleasant roe; let her breasts satisfy thee at all times; and be thou ravished always with her love.

Pro.10.12.bsb: Hatred stirs up dissension, but love covers all transgressions.
Pro.10.12.kjv: Hatred stirreth up strifes: but love covereth all sins.

Pro.15.17.bsb: Better a dish of vegetables where there is love than a fattened ox with hatred.
Pro.15.17.kjv: Better is a dinner of herbs where love is, than a stalled ox and hatred therewith.

Pro.18.14.bsb: The spirit of a man can endure his sickness, but who can survive a broken spirit?
Pro.18.14.kjv: The spirit of a man will sustain his infirmity; but a wounded spirit who can bear?

Pro.20.17.bsb: Food gained by fraud is sweet to a man, but later his mouth is full of gravel.
Pro.20.17.kjv: Bread of deceit is sweet to a man; but afterwards his mouth shall be filled with gravel.

Pro.20.24.bsb: A man’s steps are from the LORD, so how can anyone understand his own way?
Pro.20.24.kjv: Man’s goings are of the Lord; how can a man then understand his own way?

Pro.5.21.bsb: For a man’s ways are before the eyes of the LORD, and the LORD examines all his paths.
Pro.5.21.kjv: For the ways of man are before the eyes of the Lord, and he pondereth all his goings.

Pro.16.1.bsb: The plans of the heart belong to man, but the reply of the tongue is from the LORD.
Pro.16.1.kjv: The preparations of the heart in man, and the answer of the tongue, is from the Lord.

Pro.16.2.bsb: All a man’s ways are pure in his own eyes, but his motives are weighed out by the LORD.
Pro.16.2.kjv: All the ways of a man are clean in his own eyes; but the Lord weigheth the spirits.

Pro.15.8.bsb: The sacrifice of the wicked is detestable to the LORD, but the prayer of the upright is His delight.
Pro.15.8.kjv: The sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination to the Lord: but the prayer of the upright is his delight.

Pro.30.8.bsb: Keep falsehood and deceitful words far from me. Give me neither poverty nor riches; feed me with the bread that is my portion.
Pro.30.8.kjv: Remove far from me vanity and lies: give me neither poverty nor riches; feed me with food convenient for me:

Pro.1.24.bsb: Because you refused my call, and no one took my outstretched hand,
Pro.1.24.kjv: Because I have called, and ye refused; I have stretched out my hand, and no man regarded;

Pro.1.25.bsb: because you neglected all my counsel, and wanted none of my correction,
Pro.1.25.kjv: But ye have set at nought all my counsel, and would none of my reproof:

Pro.1.28.bsb: Then they will call on me, but I will not answer; they will earnestly seek me, but will not find me.
Pro.1.28.kjv: Then shall they call upon me, but I will not answer; they shall seek me early, but they shall not find me:

Pro.28.9.bsb: Whoever turns his ear away from hearing the law, even his prayer is detestable.
Pro.28.9.kjv: He that turneth away his ear from hearing the law, even his prayer shall be abomination.

Pro.21.13.bsb: Whoever shuts his ears to the cry of the poor, he too shall cry out and receive no answer.
Pro.21.13.kjv: Whoso stoppeth his ears at the cry of the poor, he also shall cry himself, but shall not be heard.

Pro.20.25.bsb: It is a trap for a man to dedicate something rashly, only later to reconsider his vows.
Pro.20.25.kjv: It is a snare to the man who devoureth that which is holy, and after vows to make enquiry.

Pro.31.1.bsb: These are the words of King Lemuel—the burden that his mother taught him:
Pro.31.1.kjv: The words of king Lemuel, the prophecy that his mother taught him.

Pro.31.2.bsb: What shall I say, O my son? What, O son of my womb? What, O son of my vows?
Pro.31.2.kjv: What, my son? and what, the son of my womb? and what, the son of my vows?

Pro.31.10.bsb: A wife of noble character, who can find? She is far more precious than rubies.
Pro.31.10.kjv: Who can find a virtuous woman? for her price is far above rubies.

Pro.31.11.bsb: The heart of her husband trusts in her, and he lacks nothing of value.
Pro.31.11.kjv: The heart of her husband doth safely trust in her, so that he shall have no need of spoil.

Pro.31.12.bsb: She brings him good and not harm all the days of her life.
Pro.31.12.kjv: She will do him good and not evil all the days of her life.

Pro.31.13.bsb: She selects wool and flax and works with eager hands.
Pro.31.13.kjv: She seeketh wool, and flax, and worketh willingly with her hands.

Pro.31.14.bsb: She is like the merchant ships, bringing her food from afar.
Pro.31.14.kjv: She is like the merchants’ ships; she bringeth her food from afar.

Pro.31.15.bsb: She rises while it is still night to provide food for her household and portions for her maidservants.
Pro.31.15.kjv: She riseth also while it is yet night, and giveth meat to her household, and a portion to her maidens.

Pro.31.16.bsb: She appraises a field and buys it; from her earnings she plants a vineyard.
Pro.31.16.kjv: She considereth a field, and buyeth it: with the fruit of her hands she planteth a vineyard.

Pro.31.17.bsb: She girds herself with strength and shows that her arms are strong.
Pro.31.17.kjv: She girdeth her loins with strength, and strengtheneth her arms.

Pro.31.18.bsb: She sees that her gain is good, and her lamp is not extinguished at night.
Pro.31.18.kjv: She perceiveth that her merchandise is good: her candle goeth not out by night.

Pro.31.19.bsb: She stretches out her hands to the distaff and grasps the spindle with her fingers.
Pro.31.19.kjv: She layeth her hands to the spindle, and her hands hold the distaff.

Pro.31.20.bsb: She opens her arms to the poor and reaches out her hands to the needy.
Pro.31.20.kjv: She stretcheth out her hand to the poor; yea, she reacheth forth her hands to the needy.

Pro.31.21.bsb: When it snows, she has no fear for her household, for they are all clothed in scarlet.
Pro.31.21.kjv: She is not afraid of the snow for her household: for all her household are clothed with scarlet.

Pro.31.22.bsb: She makes coverings for her bed; her clothing is fine linen and purple.
Pro.31.22.kjv: She maketh herself coverings of tapestry; her clothing is silk and purple.

Pro.31.23.bsb: Her husband is known at the city gates, where he sits among the elders of the land.
Pro.31.23.kjv: Her husband is known in the gates, when he sitteth among the elders of the land.

Pro.31.24.bsb: She makes linen garments and sells them; she delivers sashes to the merchants.
Pro.31.24.kjv: She maketh fine linen, and selleth it; and delivereth girdles unto the merchant.

Pro.31.25.bsb: Strength and honor are her clothing, and she can laugh at the days to come.
Pro.31.25.kjv: Strength and honour are her clothing; and she shall rejoice in time to come.

Pro.31.26.bsb: She opens her mouth with wisdom, and faithful instruction is on her tongue.
Pro.31.26.kjv: She openeth her mouth with wisdom; and in her tongue is the law of kindness.

Pro.31.27.bsb: She watches over the affairs of her household and does not eat the bread of idleness.
Pro.31.27.kjv: She looketh well to the ways of her household, and eateth not the bread of idleness.

Pro.31.28.bsb: Her children rise up and call her blessed; her husband praises her as well:
Pro.31.28.kjv: Her children arise up, and call her blessed; her husband also, and he praiseth her.

Pro.31.30.bsb: Charm is deceptive and beauty is fleeting, but a woman who fears the LORD is to be praised.
Pro.31.30.kjv: Favour is deceitful, and beauty is vain: but a woman that feareth the Lord, she shall be praised.

Pro.7.10.bsb: Then a woman came out to meet him, with the attire of a harlot and cunning of heart.
Pro.7.10.kjv: And, behold, there met him a woman with the attire of an harlot, and subtil of heart.

Pro.14.26.bsb: He who fears the LORD is secure in confidence, and his children shall have a place of refuge.
Pro.14.26.kjv: In the fear of the Lord is strong confidence: and his children shall have a place of refuge.

Pro.6.34.bsb: For jealousy enrages a husband, and he will show no mercy in the day of vengeance.
Pro.6.34.kjv: For jealousy is the rage of a man: therefore he will not spare in the day of vengeance.

Pro.12.16.bsb: A fool’s anger is known at once, but a prudent man overlooks an insult.
Pro.12.16.kjv: A fool’s wrath is presently known: but a prudent man covereth shame.

Pro.14.17.bsb: A quick-tempered man acts foolishly, and a devious man is hated.
Pro.14.17.kjv: He that is soon angry dealeth foolishly: and a man of wicked devices is hated.

Pro.14.29.bsb: A patient man has great understanding, but a quick-tempered man promotes folly.
Pro.14.29.kjv: He that is slow to wrath is of great understanding: but he that is hasty of spirit exalteth folly.

Pro.15.1.bsb: A gentle answer turns away wrath, but a harsh word stirs up anger.
Pro.15.1.kjv: A soft answer turneth away wrath: but grievous words stir up anger.

Pro.15.18.bsb: A hot-tempered man stirs up strife, but he who is slow to anger calms dispute.
Pro.15.18.kjv: A wrathful man stirreth up strife: but he that is slow to anger appeaseth strife.

Pro.16.14.bsb: The wrath of a king is a messenger of death, but a wise man will pacify it.
Pro.16.14.kjv: The wrath of a king is as messengers of death: but a wise man will pacify it.

Pro.16.29.bsb: A violent man entices his neighbor and leads him down a path that is not good.
Pro.16.29.kjv: A violent man enticeth his neighbour, and leadeth him into the way that is not good.

Pro.16.32.bsb: He who is slow to anger is better than a warrior, and he who controls his temper is greater than one who captures a city.
Pro.16.32.kjv: He that is slow to anger is better than the mighty; and he that ruleth his spirit than he that taketh a city.

Pro.17.14.bsb: To start a quarrel is to release a flood; so abandon the dispute before it breaks out.
Pro.17.14.kjv: The beginning of strife is as when one letteth out water: therefore leave off contention, before it be meddled with.

Pro.19.11.bsb: A man’s insight gives him patience, and his virtue is to overlook an offense.
Pro.19.11.kjv: The discretion of a man deferreth his anger; and it is his glory to pass over a transgression.

Pro.19.12.bsb: A king’s rage is like the roar of a lion, but his favor is like dew on the grass.
Pro.19.12.kjv: The king’s wrath is as the roaring of a lion; but his favour is as dew upon the grass.

Pro.19.19.bsb: A man of great anger must pay the penalty; if you rescue him, you will have to do so again.
Pro.19.19.kjv: A man of great wrath shall suffer punishment: for if thou deliver him, yet thou must do it again.

Pro.21.24.bsb: Mocker is the name of the proud and arrogant man—of him who acts with excessive pride.
Pro.21.24.kjv: Proud and haughty scorner is his name, who dealeth in proud wrath.

Pro.22.24.bsb: Do not make friends with an angry man, and do not associate with a hot-tempered man,
Pro.22.24.kjv: Make no friendship with an angry man; and with a furious man thou shalt not go:

Pro.22.25.bsb: or you may learn his ways and entangle yourself in a snare.
Pro.22.25.kjv: Lest thou learn his ways, and get a snare to thy soul.

Pro.25.28.bsb: Like a city whose walls are broken down is a man who does not control his temper.
Pro.25.28.kjv: He that hath no rule over his own spirit is like a city that is broken down, and without walls.

Pro.27.3.bsb: A stone is heavy and sand is a burden, but aggravation from a fool outweighs them both.
Pro.27.3.kjv: A stone is heavy, and the sand weighty; but a fool’s wrath is heavier than them both.

Pro.27.4.bsb: Wrath is cruel and anger is like a flood, but who can withstand jealousy?
Pro.27.4.kjv: Wrath is cruel, and anger is outrageous; but who is able to stand before envy?

Pro.29.8.bsb: Mockers inflame a city, but the wise turn away anger.
Pro.29.8.kjv: Scornful men bring a city into a snare: but wise men turn away wrath.

Pro.29.9.bsb: If a wise man goes to court with a fool, there will be raving and laughing with no resolution.
Pro.29.9.kjv: If a wise man contendeth with a foolish man, whether he rage or laugh, there is no rest.

Pro.29.22.bsb: An angry man stirs up dissension, and a hot-tempered man abounds in transgression.
Pro.29.22.kjv: An angry man stirreth up strife, and a furious man aboundeth in transgression.

Pro.30.33.bsb: For as the churning of milk yields butter, and the twisting of the nose draws blood, so the stirring of anger brings forth strife.”
Pro.30.33.kjv: Surely the churning of milk bringeth forth butter, and the wringing of the nose bringeth forth blood: so the forcing of wrath bringeth forth strife.

Pro.1.26.bsb: in turn I will mock your calamity; I will sneer when terror strikes you,
Pro.1.26.kjv: I also will laugh at your calamity; I will mock when your fear cometh;

Pro.2.17.bsb: who abandons the partner of her youth and forgets the covenant of her God.
Pro.2.17.kjv: Which forsaketh the guide of her youth, and forgetteth the covenant of her God.

Pro.14.14.bsb: The backslider in heart receives the fill of his own ways, but a good man is rewarded for his ways.
Pro.14.14.kjv: The backslider in heart shall be filled with his own ways: and a good man shall be satisfied from himself.

Pro.24.16.bsb: For though a righteous man may fall seven times, he still gets up; but the wicked stumble in bad times.
Pro.24.16.kjv: For a just man falleth seven times, and riseth up again: but the wicked shall fall into mischief.

Pro.26.11.bsb: As a dog returns to its vomit, so a fool repeats his folly.
Pro.26.11.kjv: As a dog returneth to his vomit, so a fool returneth to his folly.

Pro.3.27.bsb: Do not withhold good from the deserving when it is within your power to act.
Pro.3.27.kjv: Withhold not good from them to whom it is due, when it is in the power of thine hand to do it.

Pro.3.28.bsb: Do not tell your neighbor, “Come back tomorrow and I will provide”—when you already have the means.
Pro.3.28.kjv: Say not unto thy neighbour, Go, and come again, and to morrow I will give; when thou hast it by thee.

Pro.11.25.bsb: A generous soul will prosper, and he who refreshes others will himself be refreshed.
Pro.11.25.kjv: The liberal soul shall be made fat: and he that watereth shall be watered also himself.

Pro.22.9.bsb: A generous man will be blessed, for he shares his bread with the poor.
Pro.22.9.kjv: He that hath a bountiful eye shall be blessed; for he giveth of his bread to the poor.

Pro.25.21.bsb: If your enemy is hungry, give him food to eat, and if he is thirsty, give him water to drink.
Pro.25.21.kjv: If thine enemy be hungry, give him bread to eat; and if he be thirsty, give him water to drink:

Pro.25.22.bsb: For in so doing, you will heap burning coals on his head, and the LORD will reward you.
Pro.25.22.kjv: For thou shalt heap coals of fire upon his head, and the Lord shall reward thee.

Pro.28.27.bsb: Whoever gives to the poor will not be in need, but he who hides his eyes will receive many curses.
Pro.28.27.kjv: He that giveth unto the poor shall not lack: but he that hideth his eyes shall have many a curse.

Pro.30.7.bsb: Two things I ask of You—do not refuse me before I die:
Pro.30.7.kjv: Two things have I required of thee; deny me them not before I die:

Pro.30.9.bsb: Otherwise, I may have too much and deny You, saying, ‘Who is the LORD?’ Or I may become poor and steal, profaning the name of my God.
Pro.30.9.kjv: Lest I be full, and deny thee, and say, Who is the Lord? or lest I be poor, and steal, and take the name of my God in vain.

Pro.1.7.bsb: The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge, but fools despise wisdom and discipline.
Pro.1.7.kjv: The fear of the Lord is the beginning of knowledge: but fools despise wisdom and instruction.

Pro.1.22.bsb: “How long, O simple ones, will you love your simple ways? How long will scoffers delight in their scorn and fools hate knowledge?
Pro.1.22.kjv: How long, ye simple ones, will ye love simplicity? and the scorners delight in their scorning, and fools hate knowledge?

Pro.1.29.bsb: For they hated knowledge and chose not to fear the LORD.
Pro.1.29.kjv: For that they hated knowledge, and did not choose the fear of the Lord:

Pro.1.30.bsb: They accepted none of my counsel; they despised all my reproof.
Pro.1.30.kjv: They would none of my counsel: they despised all my reproof.

Pro.4.19.bsb: But the way of the wicked is like the darkest gloom; they do not know what makes them stumble.
Pro.4.19.kjv: The way of the wicked is as darkness: they know not at what they stumble.

Pro.7.7.bsb: I saw among the simple, I noticed among the youths, a young man lacking judgment,
Pro.7.7.kjv: And beheld among the simple ones, I discerned among the youths, a young man void of understanding,

Pro.7.8.bsb: crossing the street near her corner, strolling down the road to her house,
Pro.7.8.kjv: Passing through the street near her corner; and he went the way to her house,

Pro.7.9.bsb: at twilight, as the day was fading into the dark of the night.
Pro.7.9.kjv: In the twilight, in the evening, in the black and dark night:

Pro.7.11.bsb: She is loud and defiant; her feet do not remain at home.
Pro.7.11.kjv: (She is loud and stubborn; her feet abide not in her house:

Pro.7.12.bsb: Now in the street, now in the squares, she lurks at every corner.
Pro.7.12.kjv: Now is she without, now in the streets, and lieth in wait at every corner.)

Pro.7.13.bsb: She seizes him and kisses him; she brazenly says to him:
Pro.7.13.kjv: So she caught him, and kissed him, and with an impudent face said unto him,

Pro.7.14.bsb: “I have made my peace offerings; today I have paid my vows.
Pro.7.14.kjv: I have peace offerings with me; this day have I payed my vows.

Pro.7.15.bsb: So I came out to meet you; I sought you, and I have found you.
Pro.7.15.kjv: Therefore came I forth to meet thee, diligently to seek thy face, and I have found thee.

Pro.7.16.bsb: I have decked my bed with coverings, with colored linen from Egypt.
Pro.7.16.kjv: I have decked my bed with coverings of tapestry, with carved works, with fine linen of Egypt.

Pro.7.17.bsb: I have perfumed my bed with myrrh, with aloes, and with cinnamon.
Pro.7.17.kjv: I have perfumed my bed with myrrh, aloes, and cinnamon.

Pro.7.18.bsb: Come, let us take our fill of love till morning. Let us delight in loving caresses!
Pro.7.18.kjv: Come, let us take our fill of love until the morning: let us solace ourselves with loves.

Pro.7.19.bsb: For my husband is not at home; he has gone on a long journey.
Pro.7.19.kjv: For the goodman is not at home, he is gone a long journey:

Pro.7.20.bsb: He took with him a bag of money and will not return till the moon is full.”
Pro.7.20.kjv: He hath taken a bag of money with him, and will come home at the day appointed.

Pro.7.21.bsb: With her great persuasion she entices him; with her flattering lips she lures him.
Pro.7.21.kjv: With her much fair speech she caused him to yield, with the flattering of her lips she forced him.

Pro.7.22.bsb: He follows her on impulse, like an ox going to the slaughter, like a deer bounding into a trap,
Pro.7.22.kjv: He goeth after her straightway, as an ox goeth to the slaughter, or as a fool to the correction of the stocks;

Pro.7.23.bsb: until an arrow pierces his liver, like a bird darting into a snare—not knowing it will cost him his life.
Pro.7.23.kjv: Till a dart strike through his liver; as a bird hasteth to the snare, and knoweth not that it is for his life.

Pro.10.21.bsb: The lips of the righteous feed many, but fools die for lack of judgment.
Pro.10.21.kjv: The lips of the righteous feed many: but fools die for want of wisdom.

Pro.13.18.bsb: Poverty and shame come to him who ignores discipline, but whoever heeds correction is honored.
Pro.13.18.kjv: Poverty and shame shall be to him that refuseth instruction: but he that regardeth reproof shall be honoured.

Pro.14.12.bsb: There is a way that seems right to a man, but its end is the way of death.
Pro.14.12.kjv: There is a way which seemeth right unto a man, but the end thereof are the ways of death.

Pro.17.16.bsb: Why should the fool have money in his hand with no intention of buying wisdom?
Pro.17.16.kjv: Wherefore is there a price in the hand of a fool to get wisdom, seeing he hath no heart to it?

Pro.19.2.bsb: Even zeal is no good without knowledge, and he who hurries his footsteps misses the mark.
Pro.19.2.kjv: Also, that the soul be without knowledge, it is not good; and he that hasteth with his feet sinneth.

Pro.19.3.bsb: A man’s own folly subverts his way, yet his heart rages against the LORD.
Pro.19.3.kjv: The foolishness of man perverteth his way: and his heart fretteth against the Lord.

Pro.28.5.bsb: Evil men do not understand justice, but those who seek the LORD comprehend fully.
Pro.28.5.kjv: Evil men understand not judgment: but they that seek the Lord understand all things.

Pro.20.11.bsb: Even a young man is known by his actions—whether his conduct is pure and upright.
Pro.20.11.kjv: Even a child is known by his doings, whether his work be pure, and whether it be right.

Pro.17.6.bsb: Grandchildren are the crown of the aged, and the glory of a son is his father.
Pro.17.6.kjv: Children’s children are the crown of old men; and the glory of children are their fathers.

Pro.1.8.bsb: Listen, my son, to your father’s instruction, and do not forsake the teaching of your mother.
Pro.1.8.kjv: My son, hear the instruction of thy father, and forsake not the law of thy mother:

Pro.1.9.bsb: For they are a garland of grace on your head and a pendant around your neck.
Pro.1.9.kjv: For they shall be an ornament of grace unto thy head, and chains about thy neck.

Pro.3.1.bsb: My son, do not forget my teaching, but let your heart keep my commandments;
Pro.3.1.kjv: My son, forget not my law; but let thine heart keep my commandments:

Pro.3.2.bsb: for they will add length to your days, years and peace to your life.
Pro.3.2.kjv: For length of days, and long life, and peace, shall they add to thee.

Pro.3.3.bsb: Never let loving devotion or faithfulness leave you; bind them around your neck, write them on the tablet of your heart.
Pro.3.3.kjv: Let not mercy and truth forsake thee: bind them about thy neck; write them upon the table of thine heart:

Pro.4.1.bsb: Listen, my sons, to a father’s instruction; pay attention and gain understanding.
Pro.4.1.kjv: Hear, ye children, the instruction of a father, and attend to know understanding.

Pro.4.2.bsb: For I give you sound teaching; do not abandon my directive.
Pro.4.2.kjv: For I give you good doctrine, forsake ye not my law.

Pro.4.3.bsb: When I was a son to my father, tender and the only child of my mother,
Pro.4.3.kjv: For I was my father’s son, tender and only beloved in the sight of my mother.

Pro.4.4.bsb: he taught me and said, “Let your heart lay hold of my words; keep my commands and you will live.
Pro.4.4.kjv: He taught me also, and said unto me, Let thine heart retain my words: keep my commandments, and live.

Pro.4.10.bsb: Listen, my son, and receive my words, and the years of your life will be many.
Pro.4.10.kjv: Hear, O my son, and receive my sayings; and the years of thy life shall be many.

Pro.4.11.bsb: I will guide you in the way of wisdom; I will lead you on straight paths.
Pro.4.11.kjv: I have taught thee in the way of wisdom; I have led thee in right paths.

Pro.4.20.bsb: My son, pay attention to my words; incline your ear to my sayings.
Pro.4.20.kjv: My son, attend to my words; incline thine ear unto my sayings.

Pro.4.21.bsb: Do not lose sight of them; keep them within your heart.
Pro.4.21.kjv: Let them not depart from thine eyes; keep them in the midst of thine heart.

Pro.4.22.bsb: For they are life to those who find them, and health to the whole body.
Pro.4.22.kjv: For they are life unto those that find them, and health to all their flesh.

Pro.5.1.bsb: My son, pay attention to my wisdom; incline your ear to my insight,
Pro.5.1.kjv: My son, attend unto my wisdom, and bow thine ear to my understanding:

Pro.5.2.bsb: that you may maintain discretion and your lips may preserve knowledge.
Pro.5.2.kjv: That thou mayest regard discretion, and that thy lips may keep knowledge.

Pro.6.20.bsb: My son, keep your father’s commandment, and do not forsake your mother’s teaching.
Pro.6.20.kjv: My son, keep thy father’s commandment, and forsake not the law of thy mother:

Pro.6.21.bsb: Bind them always upon your heart; tie them around your neck.
Pro.6.21.kjv: Bind them continually upon thine heart, and tie them about thy neck.

Pro.6.22.bsb: When you walk, they will guide you; when you lie down, they will watch over you; when you awake, they will speak to you.
Pro.6.22.kjv: When thou goest, it shall lead thee; when thou sleepest, it shall keep thee; and when thou awakest, it shall talk with thee.

Pro.6.23.bsb: For this commandment is a lamp, this teaching is a light, and the reproofs of discipline are the way to life,
Pro.6.23.kjv: For the commandment is a lamp; and the law is light; and reproofs of instruction are the way of life:

Pro.6.24.bsb: to keep you from the evil woman, from the smooth tongue of the adulteress.
Pro.6.24.kjv: To keep thee from the evil woman, from the flattery of the tongue of a strange woman.

Pro.6.25.bsb: Do not lust in your heart for her beauty or let her captivate you with her eyes.
Pro.6.25.kjv: Lust not after her beauty in thine heart; neither let her take thee with her eyelids.

Pro.8.32.bsb: Now therefore, my sons, listen to me, for blessed are those who keep my ways.
Pro.8.32.kjv: Now therefore hearken unto me, O ye children: for blessed are they that keep my ways.

Pro.8.33.bsb: Listen to instruction and be wise; do not ignore it.
Pro.8.33.kjv: Hear instruction, and be wise, and refuse it not.

Pro.23.22.bsb: Listen to your father who gave you life, and do not despise your mother when she is old.
Pro.23.22.kjv: Hearken unto thy father that begat thee, and despise not thy mother when she is old.

Pro.23.26.bsb: My son, give me your heart, and let your eyes delight in my ways.
Pro.23.26.kjv: My son, give me thine heart, and let thine eyes observe my ways.

Pro.27.11.bsb: Be wise, my son, and bring joy to my heart, so that I can answer him who taunts me.
Pro.27.11.kjv: My son, be wise, and make my heart glad, that I may answer him that reproacheth me.

Pro.1.1.bsb: These are the proverbs of Solomon son of David, king of Israel,
Pro.1.1.kjv: The proverbs of Solomon the son of David, king of Israel;

Pro.1.4.bsb: To impart prudence to the simple and knowledge and discretion to the young,
Pro.1.4.kjv: To give subtilty to the simple, to the young man knowledge and discretion.

Pro.22.6.bsb: Train up a child in the way he should go, and when he is old he will not depart from it.
Pro.22.6.kjv: Train up a child in the way he should go: and when he is old, he will not depart from it.

Pro.3.4.bsb: Then you will find favor and high regard in the sight of God and man.
Pro.3.4.kjv: So shalt thou find favour and good understanding in the sight of God and man.

Pro.3.5.bsb: Trust in the LORD with all your heart, and lean not on your own understanding;
Pro.3.5.kjv: Trust in the Lord with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding.

Pro.3.6.bsb: in all your ways acknowledge Him, and He will make your paths straight.
Pro.3.6.kjv: In all thy ways acknowledge him, and he shall direct thy paths.

Pro.3.7.bsb: Be not wise in your own eyes; fear the LORD and turn away from evil.
Pro.3.7.kjv: Be not wise in thine own eyes: fear the Lord, and depart from evil.

Pro.3.8.bsb: This will bring healing to your body and refreshment to your bones.
Pro.3.8.kjv: It shall be health to thy navel, and marrow to thy bones.

Pro.3.9.bsb: Honor the LORD with your wealth and with the firstfruits of all your crops;
Pro.3.9.kjv: Honour the Lord with thy substance, and with the firstfruits of all thine increase:

Pro.3.10.bsb: then your barns will be filled with plenty, and your vats will overflow with new wine.
Pro.3.10.kjv: So shall thy barns be filled with plenty, and thy presses shall burst out with new wine.

Pro.8.17.bsb: I love those who love me, and those who seek me early shall find me.
Pro.8.17.kjv: I love them that love me; and those that seek me early shall find me.

Pro.23.15.bsb: My son, if your heart is wise, my own heart will indeed rejoice.
Pro.23.15.kjv: My son, if thine heart be wise, my heart shall rejoice, even mine.

Pro.23.16.bsb: My inmost being will rejoice when your lips speak what is right.
Pro.23.16.kjv: Yea, my reins shall rejoice, when thy lips speak right things.

Pro.23.24.bsb: The father of a righteous man will greatly rejoice, and he who fathers a wise son will delight in him.
Pro.23.24.kjv: The father of the righteous shall greatly rejoice: and he that begetteth a wise child shall have joy of him.

Pro.23.25.bsb: May your father and mother be glad, and may she who gave you birth rejoice!
Pro.23.25.kjv: Thy father and thy mother shall be glad, and she that bare thee shall rejoice.

Pro.29.3.bsb: A man who loves wisdom brings joy to his father, but a companion of prostitutes squanders his wealth.
Pro.29.3.kjv: Whoso loveth wisdom rejoiceth his father: but he that keepeth company with harlots spendeth his substance.

Pro.3.33.bsb: The curse of the LORD is on the house of the wicked, but He blesses the home of the righteous.
Pro.3.33.kjv: The curse of the Lord is in the house of the wicked: but he blesseth the habitation of the just.

Pro.11.21.bsb: Be assured that the wicked will not go unpunished, but the offspring of the righteous will escape.
Pro.11.21.kjv: Though hand join in hand, the wicked shall not be unpunished: but the seed of the righteous shall be delivered.

Pro.12.7.bsb: The wicked are overthrown and perish, but the house of the righteous will stand.
Pro.12.7.kjv: The wicked are overthrown, and are not: but the house of the righteous shall stand.

Pro.13.22.bsb: A good man leaves an inheritance to his children’s children, but the sinner’s wealth is passed to the righteous.
Pro.13.22.kjv: A good man leaveth an inheritance to his children’s children: and the wealth of the sinner is laid up for the just.

Pro.20.7.bsb: The righteous man walks with integrity; blessed are his children after him.
Pro.20.7.kjv: The just man walketh in his integrity: his children are blessed after him.

Pro.13.24.bsb: He who spares the rod hates his son, but he who loves him disciplines him diligently.
Pro.13.24.kjv: He that spareth his rod hateth his son: but he that loveth him chasteneth him betimes.

Pro.19.18.bsb: Discipline your son, for in that there is hope; do not be party to his death.
Pro.19.18.kjv: Chasten thy son while there is hope, and let not thy soul spare for his crying.

Pro.22.15.bsb: Foolishness is bound up in the heart of a child, but the rod of discipline drives it far from him.
Pro.22.15.kjv: Foolishness is bound in the heart of a child; but the rod of correction shall drive it far from him.

Pro.23.13.bsb: Do not withhold discipline from a child; although you strike him with a rod, he will not die.
Pro.23.13.kjv: Withhold not correction from the child: for if thou beatest him with the rod, he shall not die.

Pro.23.14.bsb: Strike him with a rod, and you will deliver his soul from Sheol.
Pro.23.14.kjv: Thou shalt beat him with the rod, and shalt deliver his soul from hell.

Pro.29.15.bsb: A rod of correction imparts wisdom, but a child left to himself disgraces his mother.
Pro.29.15.kjv: The rod and reproof give wisdom: but a child left to himself bringeth his mother to shame.

Pro.29.17.bsb: Discipline your son, and he will give you rest; he will bring delight to your soul.
Pro.29.17.kjv: Correct thy son, and he shall give thee rest; yea, he shall give delight unto thy soul.

Pro.13.1.bsb: A wise son heeds his father’s discipline, but a mocker does not listen to rebuke.
Pro.13.1.kjv: A wise son heareth his father’s instruction: but a scorner heareth not rebuke.

Pro.10.1.bsb: The proverbs of Solomon: A wise son brings joy to his father, but a foolish son grief to his mother.
Pro.10.1.kjv: The proverbs of Solomon. A wise son maketh a glad father: but a foolish son is the heaviness of his mother.

Pro.15.5.bsb: A fool rejects his father’s discipline, but whoever heeds correction is prudent.
Pro.15.5.kjv: A fool despiseth his father’s instruction: but he that regardeth reproof is prudent.

Pro.15.20.bsb: A wise son brings joy to his father, but a foolish man despises his mother.
Pro.15.20.kjv: A wise son maketh a glad father: but a foolish man despiseth his mother.

Pro.28.7.bsb: A discerning son keeps the law, but a companion of gluttons disgraces his father.
Pro.28.7.kjv: Whoso keepeth the law is a wise son: but he that is a companion of riotous men shameth his father.

Pro.17.2.bsb: A wise servant will rule over a disgraceful son and share his inheritance as one of the brothers.
Pro.17.2.kjv: A wise servant shall have rule over a son that causeth shame, and shall have part of the inheritance among the brethren.

Pro.17.21.bsb: A man fathers a fool to his own grief; the father of a fool has no joy.
Pro.17.21.kjv: He that begetteth a fool doeth it to his sorrow: and the father of a fool hath no joy.

Pro.17.25.bsb: A foolish son brings grief to his father and bitterness to her who bore him.
Pro.17.25.kjv: A foolish son is a grief to his father, and bitterness to her that bare him.

Pro.19.13.bsb: A foolish son is his father’s ruin, and a quarrelsome wife is like a constant dripping.
Pro.19.13.kjv: A foolish son is the calamity of his father: and the contentions of a wife are a continual dropping.

Pro.19.26.bsb: He who assaults his father or evicts his mother is a son who brings shame and disgrace.
Pro.19.26.kjv: He that wasteth his father, and chaseth away his mother, is a son that causeth shame, and bringeth reproach.

Pro.20.20.bsb: Whoever curses his father or mother, his lamp will be extinguished in deepest darkness.
Pro.20.20.kjv: Whoso curseth his father or his mother, his lamp shall be put out in obscure darkness.

Pro.28.24.bsb: He who robs his father or mother, saying, “It is not wrong,” is a companion to the man who destroys.
Pro.28.24.kjv: Whoso robbeth his father or his mother, and saith, It is no transgression; the same is the companion of a destroyer.

Pro.30.11.bsb: There is a generation of those who curse their fathers and do not bless their mothers.
Pro.30.11.kjv: There is a generation that curseth their father, and doth not bless their mother.

Pro.30.17.bsb: As for the eye that mocks a father and scorns obedience to a mother, may the ravens of the valley pluck it out and young vultures devour it.
Pro.30.17.kjv: The eye that mocketh at his father, and despiseth to obey his mother, the ravens of the valley shall pick it out, and the young eagles shall eat it.

Pro.14.32.bsb: The wicked man is thrown down by his own sin, but the righteous man has a refuge even in death.
Pro.14.32.kjv: The wicked is driven away in his wickedness: but the righteous hath hope in his death.

Pro.2.22.bsb: but the wicked will be cut off from the land, and the unfaithful will be uprooted.
Pro.2.22.kjv: But the wicked shall be cut off from the earth, and the transgressors shall be rooted out of it.

Pro.5.22.bsb: The iniquities of a wicked man entrap him; the cords of his sin entangle him.
Pro.5.22.kjv: His own iniquities shall take the wicked himself, and he shall be holden with the cords of his sins.

Pro.5.23.bsb: He dies for lack of discipline, led astray by his own great folly.
Pro.5.23.kjv: He shall die without instruction; and in the greatness of his folly he shall go astray.

Pro.10.25.bsb: When the whirlwind passes, the wicked are no more, but the righteous are secure forever.
Pro.10.25.kjv: As the whirlwind passeth, so is the wicked no more: but the righteous is an everlasting foundation.

Pro.10.27.bsb: The fear of the LORD prolongs life, but the years of the wicked will be cut short.
Pro.10.27.kjv: The fear of the Lord prolongeth days: but the years of the wicked shall be shortened.

Pro.11.7.bsb: When the wicked man dies, his hope perishes, and the hope of his strength vanishes.
Pro.11.7.kjv: When a wicked man dieth, his expectation shall perish: and the hope of unjust men perisheth.

Pro.11.10.bsb: When the righteous thrive, the city rejoices, and when the wicked perish, there are shouts of joy.
Pro.11.10.kjv: When it goeth well with the righteous, the city rejoiceth: and when the wicked perish, there is shouting.

Pro.13.9.bsb: The light of the righteous shines brightly, but the lamp of the wicked is extinguished.
Pro.13.9.kjv: The light of the righteous rejoiceth: but the lamp of the wicked shall be put out.

Pro.21.16.bsb: The man who strays from the path of understanding will rest in the assembly of the dead.
Pro.21.16.kjv: The man that wandereth out of the way of understanding shall remain in the congregation of the dead.

Pro.24.20.bsb: For the evil man has no future; the lamp of the wicked will be extinguished.
Pro.24.20.kjv: For there shall be no reward to the evil man; the candle of the wicked shall be put out.

Pro.29.1.bsb: A man who remains stiff-necked after much reproof will suddenly be shattered beyond recovery.
Pro.29.1.kjv: He, that being often reproved hardeneth his neck, shall suddenly be destroyed, and that without remedy.

Pro.29.16.bsb: When the wicked thrive, rebellion increases; but the righteous will see their downfall.
Pro.29.16.kjv: When the wicked are multiplied, transgression increaseth: but the righteous shall see their fall.

Pro.10.20.bsb: The tongue of the righteous is choice silver, but the heart of the wicked has little worth.
Pro.10.20.kjv: The tongue of the just is as choice silver: the heart of the wicked is little worth.

Pro.20.6.bsb: Many a man proclaims his loving devotion, but who can find a trustworthy man?
Pro.20.6.kjv: Most men will proclaim every one his own goodness: but a faithful man who can find?

Pro.21.8.bsb: The way of a guilty man is crooked, but the conduct of the innocent is upright.
Pro.21.8.kjv: The way of man is froward and strange: but as for the pure, his work is right.

Pro.3.31.bsb: Do not envy a violent man or choose any of his ways;
Pro.3.31.kjv: Envy thou not the oppressor, and choose none of his ways.

Pro.14.30.bsb: A tranquil heart is life to the body, but envy rots the bones.
Pro.14.30.kjv: A sound heart is the life of the flesh: but envy the rottenness of the bones.

Pro.23.17.bsb: Do not let your heart envy sinners, but always continue in the fear of the LORD.
Pro.23.17.kjv: Let not thine heart envy sinners: but be thou in the fear of the Lord all the day long.

Pro.24.1.bsb: Do not envy wicked men or desire their company;
Pro.24.1.kjv: Be not thou envious against evil men, neither desire to be with them.

Pro.24.19.bsb: Do not fret over evildoers, and do not be envious of the wicked.
Pro.24.19.kjv: Fret not thyself because of evil men, neither be thou envious at the wicked;

Pro.22.19.bsb: So that your trust may be in the LORD, I instruct you today—yes, you.
Pro.22.19.kjv: That thy trust may be in the Lord, I have made known to thee this day, even to thee.

Pro.28.25.bsb: A greedy man stirs up strife, but he who trusts in the LORD will prosper.
Pro.28.25.kjv: He that is of a proud heart stirreth up strife: but he that putteth his trust in the Lord shall be made fat.

Pro.29.25.bsb: The fear of man is a snare, but whoever trusts in the LORD is set securely on high.
Pro.29.25.kjv: The fear of man bringeth a snare: but whoso putteth his trust in the Lord shall be safe.

Pro.30.5.bsb: Every word of God is flawless; He is a shield to those who take refuge in Him.
Pro.30.5.kjv: Every word of God is pure: he is a shield unto them that put their trust in him.

Pro.3.24.bsb: When you lie down, you will not be afraid; when you rest, your sleep will be sweet.
Pro.3.24.kjv: When thou liest down, thou shalt not be afraid: yea, thou shalt lie down, and thy sleep shall be sweet.

Pro.3.25.bsb: Do not fear sudden danger or the ruin that overtakes the wicked,
Pro.3.25.kjv: Be not afraid of sudden fear, neither of the desolation of the wicked, when it cometh.

Pro.3.26.bsb: for the LORD will be your confidence and will keep your foot from the snare.
Pro.3.26.kjv: For the Lord shall be thy confidence, and shall keep thy foot from being taken.

Pro.16.3.bsb: Commit your works to the LORD and your plans will be achieved.
Pro.16.3.kjv: Commit thy works unto the Lord, and thy thoughts shall be established.

Pro.11.22.bsb: Like a gold ring in a pig’s snout is a beautiful woman who lacks discretion.
Pro.11.22.kjv: As a jewel of gold in a swine’s snout, so is a fair woman which is without discretion.

Pro.12.4.bsb: A wife of noble character is her husband’s crown, but she who causes shame is like decay in his bones.
Pro.12.4.kjv: A virtuous woman is a crown to her husband: but she that maketh ashamed is as rottenness in his bones.

Pro.14.1.bsb: Every wise woman builds her house, but a foolish one tears it down with her own hands.
Pro.14.1.kjv: Every wise woman buildeth her house: but the foolish plucketh it down with her hands.

Pro.18.19.bsb: An offended brother is harder to win than a fortified city, and disputes are like the bars of a castle.
Pro.18.19.kjv: A brother offended is harder to be won than a strong city: and their contentions are like the bars of a castle.

Pro.21.9.bsb: Better to live on a corner of the roof than to share a house with a quarrelsome wife.
Pro.21.9.kjv: It is better to dwell in a corner of the housetop, than with a brawling woman in a wide house.

Pro.21.19.bsb: Better to live in the desert than with a contentious and ill-tempered wife.
Pro.21.19.kjv: It is better to dwell in the wilderness, than with a contentious and an angry woman.

Pro.25.24.bsb: Better to live on a corner of the roof than to share a house with a quarrelsome wife.
Pro.25.24.kjv: It is better to dwell in the corner of the housetop, than with a brawling woman and in a wide house.

Pro.27.15.bsb: A constant dripping on a rainy day and a contentious woman are alike—
Pro.27.15.kjv: A continual dropping in a very rainy day and a contentious woman are alike.

Pro.27.16.bsb: restraining her is like holding back the wind or grasping oil with one’s right hand.
Pro.27.16.kjv: Whosoever hideth her hideth the wind, and the ointment of his right hand, which bewrayeth itself.

Pro.30.21.bsb: Under three things the earth trembles, under four it cannot bear up:
Pro.30.21.kjv: For three things the earth is disquieted, and for four which it cannot bear:

Pro.30.23.bsb: an unloved woman who marries, and a maidservant who supplants her mistress.
Pro.30.23.kjv: For an odious woman when she is married; and an handmaid that is heir to her mistress.

Pro.3.19.bsb: The LORD founded the earth by wisdom and established the heavens by understanding.
Pro.3.19.kjv: The Lord by wisdom hath founded the earth; by understanding hath he established the heavens.

Pro.8.26.bsb: before He made the land or fields, or any of the dust of the earth.
Pro.8.26.kjv: While as yet he had not made the earth, nor the fields, nor the highest part of the dust of the world.

Pro.8.27.bsb: I was there when He established the heavens, when He inscribed a circle on the face of the deep,
Pro.8.27.kjv: When he prepared the heavens, I was there: when he set a compass upon the face of the depth:

Pro.8.28.bsb: when He established the clouds above, when the fountains of the deep gushed forth,
Pro.8.28.kjv: When he established the clouds above: when he strengthened the fountains of the deep:

Pro.8.29.bsb: when He set a boundary for the sea, so that the waters would not surpass His command, when He marked out the foundations of the earth.
Pro.8.29.kjv: When he gave to the sea his decree, that the waters should not pass his commandment: when he appointed the foundations of the earth:

Pro.22.2.bsb: The rich and the poor have this in common: The LORD is Maker of them all.
Pro.22.2.kjv: The rich and poor meet together: the Lord is the maker of them all.

Pro.30.4.bsb: Who has ascended to heaven and come down? Who has gathered the wind in His hands? Who has bound up the waters in His cloak? Who has established all the ends of the earth? What is His name, and what is the name of His Son—surely you know!
Pro.30.4.kjv: Who hath ascended up into heaven, or descended? who hath gathered the wind in his fists? who hath bound the waters in a garment? who hath established all the ends of the earth? what is his name, and what is his son’s name, if thou canst tell?

Pro.20.12.bsb: Ears that hear and eyes that see—the LORD has made them both.
Pro.20.12.kjv: The hearing ear, and the seeing eye, the Lord hath made even both of them.

Pro.8.23.bsb: From everlasting I was established, from the beginning, before the earth began.
Pro.8.23.kjv: I was set up from everlasting, from the beginning, or ever the earth was.

Pro.8.24.bsb: When there were no watery depths, I was brought forth, when no springs were overflowing with water.
Pro.8.24.kjv: When there were no depths, I was brought forth; when there were no fountains abounding with water.

Pro.8.25.bsb: Before the mountains were settled, before the hills, I was brought forth,
Pro.8.25.kjv: Before the mountains were settled, before the hills was I brought forth:

Pro.3.23.bsb: Then you will go on your way in safety, and your foot will not stumble.
Pro.3.23.kjv: Then shalt thou walk in thy way safely, and thy foot shall not stumble.

Pro.3.32.bsb: for the LORD detests the perverse, but He is a friend to the upright.
Pro.3.32.kjv: For the froward is abomination to the Lord: but his secret is with the righteous.

Pro.8.35.bsb: For whoever finds me finds life and obtains the favor of the LORD.
Pro.8.35.kjv: For whoso findeth me findeth life, and shall obtain favour of the Lord.

Pro.10.22.bsb: The blessing of the LORD enriches, and He adds no sorrow to it.
Pro.10.22.kjv: The blessing of the Lord, it maketh rich, and he addeth no sorrow with it.

Pro.10.24.bsb: What the wicked man dreads will overtake him, but the desire of the righteous will be granted.
Pro.10.24.kjv: The fear of the wicked, it shall come upon him: but the desire of the righteous shall be granted.

Pro.11.20.bsb: The perverse in heart are an abomination to the LORD, but the blameless in their walk are His delight.
Pro.11.20.kjv: They that are of a froward heart are abomination to the Lord: but such as are upright in their way are his delight.

Pro.11.27.bsb: He who searches out good finds favor, but evil will come to him who seeks it.
Pro.11.27.kjv: He that diligently seeketh good procureth favour: but he that seeketh mischief, it shall come unto him.

Pro.12.2.bsb: The good man obtains favor from the LORD, but the LORD condemns a man who devises evil.
Pro.12.2.kjv: A good man obtaineth favour of the Lord: but a man of wicked devices will he condemn.

Pro.14.9.bsb: Fools mock the making of amends, but goodwill is found among the upright.
Pro.14.9.kjv: Fools make a mock at sin: but among the righteous there is favour.

Pro.16.7.bsb: When a man’s ways please the LORD, He makes even the man’s enemies live at peace with him.
Pro.16.7.kjv: When a man’s ways please the Lord, he maketh even his enemies to be at peace with him.

Pro.8.20.bsb: I walk in the way of righteousness, along the paths of justice,
Pro.8.20.kjv: I lead in the way of righteousness, in the midst of the paths of judgment:

Pro.9.10.bsb: The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom, and knowledge of the Holy One is understanding.
Pro.9.10.kjv: The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom: and the knowledge of the holy is understanding.

Pro.19.21.bsb: Many plans are in a man’s heart, but the purpose of the LORD will prevail.
Pro.19.21.kjv: There are many devices in a man’s heart; nevertheless the counsel of the Lord, that shall stand.

Pro.11.31.bsb: If the righteous receive their due on earth, how much more the ungodly and the sinner!
Pro.11.31.kjv: Behold, the righteous shall be recompensed in the earth: much more the wicked and the sinner.

Pro.17.3.bsb: A crucible for silver and a furnace for gold, but the LORD is the tester of hearts.
Pro.17.3.kjv: The fining pot is for silver, and the furnace for gold: but the Lord trieth the hearts.

Pro.21.2.bsb: All a man’s ways seem right to him, but the LORD weighs the heart.
Pro.21.2.kjv: Every way of a man is right in his own eyes: but the Lord pondereth the hearts.

Pro.21.3.bsb: To do righteousness and justice is more desirable to the LORD than sacrifice.
Pro.21.3.kjv: To do justice and judgment is more acceptable to the Lord than sacrifice.

Pro.24.12.bsb: If you say, “Behold, we did not know about this,” does not He who weighs hearts consider it? Does not the One who guards your life know? Will He not repay a man according to his deeds?
Pro.24.12.kjv: If thou sayest, Behold, we knew it not; doth not he that pondereth the heart consider it? and he that keepeth thy soul, doth not he know it? and shall not he render to every man according to his works?

Pro.29.13.bsb: The poor man and the oppressor have this in common: The LORD gives light to the eyes of both.
Pro.29.13.kjv: The poor and the deceitful man meet together: the Lord lighteneth both their eyes.

Pro.29.26.bsb: Many seek the ruler’s favor, but a man receives justice from the LORD.
Pro.29.26.kjv: Many seek the ruler’s favour; but every man’s judgment cometh from the Lord.

Pro.3.20.bsb: By His knowledge the watery depths were broken open, and the clouds dripped with dew.
Pro.3.20.kjv: By his knowledge the depths are broken up, and the clouds drop down the dew.

Pro.15.3.bsb: The eyes of the LORD are in every place, observing the evil and the good.
Pro.15.3.kjv: The eyes of the Lord are in every place, beholding the evil and the good.

Pro.15.11.bsb: Sheol and Abaddon lie open before the LORD—how much more the hearts of men!
Pro.15.11.kjv: Hell and destruction are before the Lord: how much more then the hearts of the children of men?

Pro.1.27.bsb: when your dread comes like a storm, and your destruction like a whirlwind, when distress and anguish overwhelm you.
Pro.1.27.kjv: When your fear cometh as desolation, and your destruction cometh as a whirlwind; when distress and anguish cometh upon you.

Pro.15.9.bsb: The LORD detests the way of the wicked, but He loves those who pursue righteousness.
Pro.15.9.kjv: The way of the wicked is an abomination unto the Lord: but he loveth him that followeth after righteousness.

Pro.16.6.bsb: By loving devotion and faithfulness iniquity is atoned for, and by the fear of the LORD one turns aside from evil.
Pro.16.6.kjv: By mercy and truth iniquity is purged: and by the fear of the Lord men depart from evil.

Pro.28.13.bsb: He who conceals his sins will not prosper, but whoever confesses and renounces them will find mercy.
Pro.28.13.kjv: He that covereth his sins shall not prosper: but whoso confesseth and forsaketh them shall have mercy.

Pro.21.30.bsb: There is no wisdom, no understanding, no counsel that can prevail against the LORD.
Pro.21.30.kjv: There is no wisdom nor understanding nor counsel against the Lord.

Pro.2.7.bsb: He stores up sound wisdom for the upright; He is a shield to those who walk with integrity,
Pro.2.7.kjv: He layeth up sound wisdom for the righteous: he is a buckler to them that walk uprightly.

Pro.2.8.bsb: to guard the paths of justice and protect the way of His saints.
Pro.2.8.kjv: He keepeth the paths of judgment, and preserveth the way of his saints.

Pro.10.3.bsb: The LORD does not let the righteous go hungry, but He denies the craving of the wicked.
Pro.10.3.kjv: The Lord will not suffer the soul of the righteous to famish: but he casteth away the substance of the wicked.

Pro.10.30.bsb: The righteous will never be shaken, but the wicked will not inhabit the land.
Pro.10.30.kjv: The righteous shall never be removed: but the wicked shall not inhabit the earth.

Pro.11.8.bsb: The righteous man is delivered from trouble; in his place the wicked man goes in.
Pro.11.8.kjv: The righteous is delivered out of trouble, and the wicked cometh in his stead.

Pro.12.3.bsb: A man cannot be established through wickedness, but the righteous cannot be uprooted.
Pro.12.3.kjv: A man shall not be established by wickedness: but the root of the righteous shall not be moved.

Pro.12.13.bsb: An evil man is trapped by his rebellious speech, but a righteous man escapes from trouble.
Pro.12.13.kjv: The wicked is snared by the transgression of his lips: but the just shall come out of trouble.

Pro.12.21.bsb: No harm befalls the righteous, but the wicked are filled with trouble.
Pro.12.21.kjv: There shall no evil happen to the just: but the wicked shall be filled with mischief.

Pro.15.19.bsb: The way of the slacker is like a hedge of thorns, but the path of the upright is a highway.
Pro.15.19.kjv: The way of the slothful man is as an hedge of thorns: but the way of the righteous is made plain.

Pro.16.9.bsb: A man’s heart plans his course, but the LORD determines his steps.
Pro.16.9.kjv: A man’s heart deviseth his way: but the Lord directeth his steps.

Pro.16.33.bsb: The lot is cast into the lap, but its every decision is from the LORD.
Pro.16.33.kjv: The lot is cast into the lap; but the whole disposing thereof is of the Lord.

Pro.19.23.bsb: The fear of the LORD leads to life, that one may rest content, without visitation from harm.
Pro.19.23.kjv: The fear of the Lord tendeth to life: and he that hath it shall abide satisfied; he shall not be visited with evil.

Pro.20.22.bsb: Do not say, “I will avenge this evil!” Wait on the LORD, and He will save you.
Pro.20.22.kjv: Say not thou, I will recompense evil; but wait on the Lord, and he shall save thee.

Pro.21.31.bsb: A horse is prepared for the day of battle, but victory is of the LORD.
Pro.21.31.kjv: The horse is prepared against the day of battle: but safety is of the Lord.

Pro.22.12.bsb: The LORD’s eyes keep watch over knowledge, but He frustrates the words of the faithless.
Pro.22.12.kjv: The eyes of the Lord preserve knowledge, and he overthroweth the words of the transgressor.

Pro.2.21.bsb: For the upright will inhabit the land, and the blameless will remain in it;
Pro.2.21.kjv: For the upright shall dwell in the land, and the perfect shall remain in it.

Pro.11.11.bsb: By the blessing of the upright a city is built up, but by the mouth of the wicked it is torn down.
Pro.11.11.kjv: By the blessing of the upright the city is exalted: but it is overthrown by the mouth of the wicked.

Pro.13.25.bsb: A righteous man eats to his heart’s content, but the stomach of the wicked is empty.
Pro.13.25.kjv: The righteous eateth to the satisfying of his soul: but the belly of the wicked shall want.

Pro.14.11.bsb: The house of the wicked will be destroyed, but the tent of the upright will flourish.
Pro.14.11.kjv: The house of the wicked shall be overthrown: but the tabernacle of the upright shall flourish.

Pro.14.19.bsb: The evil bow before the good, and the wicked at the gates of the righteous.
Pro.14.19.kjv: The evil bow before the good; and the wicked at the gates of the righteous.

Pro.14.34.bsb: Righteousness exalts a nation, but sin is a disgrace to any people.
Pro.14.34.kjv: Righteousness exalteth a nation: but sin is a reproach to any people.

Pro.15.6.bsb: The house of the righteous has great treasure, but the income of the wicked is trouble.
Pro.15.6.kjv: In the house of the righteous is much treasure: but in the revenues of the wicked is trouble.

Pro.28.10.bsb: He who leads the upright along the path of evil will fall into his own pit, but the blameless will inherit what is good.
Pro.28.10.kjv: Whoso causeth the righteous to go astray in an evil way, he shall fall himself into his own pit: but the upright shall have good things in possession.

Pro.21.1.bsb: The king’s heart is a waterway in the hand of the LORD; He directs it where He pleases.
Pro.21.1.kjv: The king’s heart is in the hand of the Lord, as the rivers of water: he turneth it whithersoever he will.

Pro.21.18.bsb: The wicked become a ransom for the righteous, and the faithless for the upright.
Pro.21.18.kjv: The wicked shall be a ransom for the righteous, and the transgressor for the upright.

Pro.28.8.bsb: He who increases his wealth by interest and usury lays it up for one who is kind to the poor.
Pro.28.8.kjv: He that by usury and unjust gain increaseth his substance, he shall gather it for him that will pity the poor.

Pro.25.2.bsb: It is the glory of God to conceal a matter and the glory of kings to search it out.
Pro.25.2.kjv: It is the glory of God to conceal a thing: but the honour of kings is to search out a matter.

Pro.8.12.bsb: I, wisdom, dwell together with prudence, and I find knowledge and discretion.
Pro.8.12.kjv: I wisdom dwell with prudence, and find out knowledge of witty inventions.

Pro.8.22.bsb: The LORD created me as His first course, before His works of old.
Pro.8.22.kjv: The Lord possessed me in the beginning of his way, before his works of old.

Pro.8.30.bsb: Then I was a skilled craftsman at His side, and His delight day by day, rejoicing always in His presence.
Pro.8.30.kjv: Then I was by him, as one brought up with him: and I was daily his delight, rejoicing always before him;

Pro.8.31.bsb: I was rejoicing in His whole world, delighting together in the sons of men.
Pro.8.31.kjv: Rejoicing in the habitable part of his earth; and my delights were with the sons of men.

Pro.8.15.bsb: By me kings reign, and rulers enact just laws;
Pro.8.15.kjv: By me kings reign, and princes decree justice.

Pro.5.15.bsb: Drink water from your own cistern, and running water from your own well.
Pro.5.15.kjv: Drink waters out of thine own cistern, and running waters out of thine own well.

Pro.5.16.bsb: Why should your springs flow in the streets, your streams of water in the public squares?
Pro.5.16.kjv: Let thy fountains be dispersed abroad, and rivers of waters in the streets.

Pro.5.17.bsb: Let them be yours alone, never to be shared with strangers.
Pro.5.17.kjv: Let them be only thine own, and not strangers’ with thee.

Pro.5.18.bsb: May your fountain be blessed, and may you rejoice in the wife of your youth:
Pro.5.18.kjv: Let thy fountain be blessed: and rejoice with the wife of thy youth.

Pro.7.6.bsb: For at the window of my house I looked through the lattice.
Pro.7.6.kjv: For at the window of my house I looked through my casement,

Pro.8.5.bsb: O simple ones, learn to be shrewd; O fools, gain understanding.
Pro.8.5.kjv: O ye simple, understand wisdom: and, ye fools, be ye of an understanding heart.

Pro.9.14.bsb: She sits at the door of her house, on a seat in the heights of the city,
Pro.9.14.kjv: For she sitteth at the door of her house, on a seat in the high places of the city,

Pro.9.15.bsb: calling out to those who pass by, who make their paths straight.
Pro.9.15.kjv: To call passengers who go right on their ways:

Pro.9.16.bsb: “Whoever is simple, let him turn in here!” she says to him who lacks judgment.
Pro.9.16.kjv: Whoso is simple, let him turn in hither: and as for him that wanteth understanding, she saith to him,

Pro.9.17.bsb: “Stolen water is sweet, and bread eaten in secret is tasty!”
Pro.9.17.kjv: Stolen waters are sweet, and bread eaten in secret is pleasant.

Pro.9.18.bsb: But they do not know that the dead are there, that her guests are in the depths of Sheol.
Pro.9.18.kjv: But he knoweth not that the dead are there; and that her guests are in the depths of hell.

Pro.22.3.bsb: The prudent see danger and take cover, but the simple keep going and suffer the consequences.
Pro.22.3.kjv: A prudent man foreseeth the evil, and hideth himself: but the simple pass on, and are punished.

Pro.27.1.bsb: Do not boast about tomorrow, for you do not know what a day may bring.
Pro.27.1.kjv: Boast not thyself of to morrow; for thou knowest not what a day may bring forth.

Pro.27.12.bsb: The prudent see danger and take cover, but the simple keep going and pay the penalty.
Pro.27.12.kjv: A prudent man foreseeth the evil, and hideth himself; but the simple pass on, and are punished.

Pro.24.30.bsb: I went past the field of a slacker and by the vineyard of a man lacking judgment.
Pro.24.30.kjv: I went by the field of the slothful, and by the vineyard of the man void of understanding;

Pro.24.31.bsb: Thorns had grown up everywhere, thistles had covered the ground, and the stone wall was broken down.
Pro.24.31.kjv: And, lo, it was all grown over with thorns, and nettles had covered the face thereof, and the stone wall thereof was broken down.

Pro.24.32.bsb: I observed and took it to heart; I looked and received instruction:
Pro.24.32.kjv: Then I saw, and considered it well: I looked upon it, and received instruction.

Pro.24.33.bsb: A little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to rest,
Pro.24.33.kjv: Yet a little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to sleep:

Pro.24.34.bsb: and poverty will come upon you like a robber, and need like a bandit.
Pro.24.34.kjv: So shall thy poverty come as one that travelleth; and thy want as an armed man.

Pro.12.14.bsb: By fruitful speech a man is filled with good things, and the work of his hands returns to him.
Pro.12.14.kjv: A man shall be satisfied with good by the fruit of his mouth: and the recompence of a man’s hands shall be rendered unto him.

Pro.24.11.bsb: Rescue those being led away to death, and restrain those stumbling toward the slaughter.
Pro.24.11.kjv: If thou forbear to deliver them that are drawn unto death, and those that are ready to be slain;

Pro.11.24.bsb: One gives freely, yet gains even more; another withholds what is right, only to become poor.
Pro.11.24.kjv: There is that scattereth, and yet increaseth; and there is that withholdeth more than is meet, but it tendeth to poverty.

Pro.13.7.bsb: One pretends to be rich, but has nothing; another pretends to be poor, yet has great wealth.
Pro.13.7.kjv: There is that maketh himself rich, yet hath nothing: there is that maketh himself poor, yet hath great riches.

Pro.14.21.bsb: He who despises his neighbor sins, but blessed is he who shows kindness to the poor.
Pro.14.21.kjv: He that despiseth his neighbour sinneth: but he that hath mercy on the poor, happy is he.

Pro.19.6.bsb: Many seek the favor of the prince, and everyone is a friend of the gift giver.
Pro.19.6.kjv: Many will intreat the favour of the prince: and every man is a friend to him that giveth gifts.

Pro.19.17.bsb: Kindness to the poor is a loan to the LORD, and He will repay the lender.
Pro.19.17.kjv: He that hath pity upon the poor lendeth unto the Lord; and that which he hath given will he pay him again.

Pro.21.26.bsb: All day long he covets more, but the righteous give without restraint.
Pro.21.26.kjv: He coveteth greedily all the day long: but the righteous giveth and spareth not.

Pro.4.16.bsb: For they cannot sleep unless they do evil; they are deprived of slumber until they make someone fall.
Pro.4.16.kjv: For they sleep not, except they have done mischief; and their sleep is taken away, unless they cause some to fall.

Pro.4.17.bsb: For they eat the bread of wickedness and drink the wine of violence.
Pro.4.17.kjv: For they eat the bread of wickedness, and drink the wine of violence.

Pro.6.14.bsb: With deceit in his heart he devises evil; he continually sows discord.
Pro.6.14.kjv: Frowardness is in his heart, he deviseth mischief continually; he soweth discord.

Pro.6.15.bsb: Therefore calamity will come upon him suddenly; in an instant he will be shattered beyond recovery.
Pro.6.15.kjv: Therefore shall his calamity come suddenly; suddenly shall he be broken without remedy.

Pro.6.16.bsb: There are six things that the LORD hates, seven that are detestable to Him:
Pro.6.16.kjv: These six things doth the Lord hate: yea, seven are an abomination unto him:

Pro.6.18.bsb: a heart that devises wicked schemes, feet that run swiftly to evil,
Pro.6.18.kjv: An heart that deviseth wicked imaginations, feet that be swift in running to mischief,

Pro.6.19.bsb: a false witness who gives false testimony, and one who stirs up discord among brothers.
Pro.6.19.kjv: A false witness that speaketh lies, and he that soweth discord among brethren.

Pro.11.17.bsb: A kind man benefits himself, but a cruel man brings trouble on himself.
Pro.11.17.kjv: The merciful man doeth good to his own soul: but he that is cruel troubleth his own flesh.

Pro.12.10.bsb: A righteous man regards the life of his animal, but the tender mercies of the wicked are only cruelty.
Pro.12.10.kjv: A righteous man regardeth the life of his beast: but the tender mercies of the wicked are cruel.

Pro.14.22.bsb: Do not those who contrive evil go astray? But those who plan goodness find loving devotion and faithfulness.
Pro.14.22.kjv: Do they not err that devise evil? but mercy and truth shall be to them that devise good.

Pro.16.30.bsb: He who winks his eye devises perversity; he who purses his lips is bent on evil.
Pro.16.30.kjv: He shutteth his eyes to devise froward things: moving his lips he bringeth evil to pass.

Pro.17.5.bsb: He who mocks the poor insults their Maker; whoever gloats over calamity will not go unpunished.
Pro.17.5.kjv: Whoso mocketh the poor reproacheth his Maker: and he that is glad at calamities shall not be unpunished.

Pro.21.10.bsb: The soul of the wicked man craves evil; his neighbor finds no favor in his eyes.
Pro.21.10.kjv: The soul of the wicked desireth evil: his neighbour findeth no favour in his eyes.

Pro.24.8.bsb: He who plots evil will be called a schemer.
Pro.24.8.kjv: He that deviseth to do evil shall be called a mischievous person.

Pro.24.17.bsb: Do not gloat when your enemy falls, and do not let your heart rejoice when he stumbles,
Pro.24.17.kjv: Rejoice not when thine enemy falleth, and let not thine heart be glad when he stumbleth:

Pro.24.18.bsb: or the LORD will see and disapprove, and turn His wrath away from him.
Pro.24.18.kjv: Lest the Lord see it, and it displease him, and he turn away his wrath from him.

Pro.24.29.bsb: Do not say, “I will do to him as he has done to me; I will repay the man according to his work.”
Pro.24.29.kjv: Say not, I will do so to him as he hath done to me: I will render to the man according to his work.

Pro.26.2.bsb: Like a fluttering sparrow or darting swallow, an undeserved curse does not come to rest.
Pro.26.2.kjv: As the bird by wandering, as the swallow by flying, so the curse causeless shall not come.

Pro.26.27.bsb: He who digs a pit will fall into it, and he who rolls a stone will have it roll back on him.
Pro.26.27.kjv: Whoso diggeth a pit shall fall therein: and he that rolleth a stone, it will return upon him.

Pro.30.14.bsb: there is a generation whose teeth are swords and whose jaws are knives, devouring the oppressed from the earth and the needy from among men.
Pro.30.14.kjv: There is a generation, whose teeth are as swords, and their jaw teeth as knives, to devour the poor from off the earth, and the needy from among men.

Pro.20.27.bsb: The spirit of a man is the lamp of the LORD, searching out his inmost being.
Pro.20.27.kjv: The spirit of man is the candle of the Lord, searching all the inward parts of the belly.

Pro.18.22.bsb: He who finds a wife finds a good thing and obtains favor from the LORD.
Pro.18.22.kjv: Whoso findeth a wife findeth a good thing, and obtaineth favour of the Lord.

Pro.25.20.bsb: Like one who removes a garment on a cold day or vinegar poured on a wound is one who sings songs to a heavy heart.
Pro.25.20.kjv: As he that taketh away a garment in cold weather, and as vinegar upon nitre, so is he that singeth songs to an heavy heart.

Pro.3.29.bsb: Do not devise evil against your neighbor, for he trustfully dwells beside you.
Pro.3.29.kjv: Devise not evil against thy neighbour, seeing he dwelleth securely by thee.

Pro.23.10.bsb: Do not move an ancient boundary stone or encroach on the fields of the fatherless,
Pro.23.10.kjv: Remove not the old landmark; and enter not into the fields of the fatherless:

Pro.3.12.bsb: for the LORD disciplines the one He loves, as does a father the son in whom he delights.
Pro.3.12.kjv: For whom the Lord loveth he correcteth; even as a father the son in whom he delighteth.

Pro.10.15.bsb: The wealth of the rich man is his fortified city, but poverty is the ruin of the poor.
Pro.10.15.kjv: The rich man’s wealth is his strong city: the destruction of the poor is their poverty.

Pro.13.8.bsb: Riches may ransom a man’s life, but a poor man hears no threat.
Pro.13.8.kjv: The ransom of a man’s life are his riches: but the poor heareth not rebuke.

Pro.13.23.bsb: Abundant food is in the fallow ground of the poor, but without justice it is swept away.
Pro.13.23.kjv: Much food is in the tillage of the poor: but there is that is destroyed for want of judgment.

Pro.14.20.bsb: The poor man is hated even by his neighbor, but many are those who love the rich.
Pro.14.20.kjv: The poor is hated even of his own neighbour: but the rich hath many friends.

Pro.14.31.bsb: Whoever oppresses the poor taunts their Maker, but whoever is kind to the needy honors Him.
Pro.14.31.kjv: He that oppresseth the poor reproacheth his Maker: but he that honoureth him hath mercy on the poor.

Pro.18.23.bsb: The poor man pleads for mercy, but the rich man answers harshly.
Pro.18.23.kjv: The poor useth intreaties; but the rich answereth roughly.

Pro.19.1.bsb: Better a poor man who walks with integrity than a fool whose lips are perverse.
Pro.19.1.kjv: Better is the poor that walketh in his integrity, than he that is perverse in his lips, and is a fool.

Pro.19.4.bsb: Wealth attracts many friends, but a poor man is deserted by his friend.
Pro.19.4.kjv: Wealth maketh many friends; but the poor is separated from his neighbour.

Pro.19.7.bsb: All the brothers of a poor man hate him—how much more do his friends avoid him! He may pursue them with pleading, but they are nowhere to be found.
Pro.19.7.kjv: All the brethren of the poor do hate him: how much more do his friends go far from him? he pursueth them with words, yet they are wanting to him.

Pro.19.22.bsb: The desire of a man is loving devotion; better to be poor than a liar.
Pro.19.22.kjv: The desire of a man is his kindness: and a poor man is better than a liar.

Pro.20.13.bsb: Do not love sleep, or you will grow poor; open your eyes, and you will have plenty of food.
Pro.20.13.kjv: Love not sleep, lest thou come to poverty; open thine eyes, and thou shalt be satisfied with bread.

Pro.23.21.bsb: For the drunkard and the glutton will come to poverty, and drowsiness will clothe them in rags.
Pro.23.21.kjv: For the drunkard and the glutton shall come to poverty: and drowsiness shall clothe a man with rags.

Pro.28.6.bsb: Better a poor man who walks with integrity than a rich man whose ways are perverse.
Pro.28.6.kjv: Better is the poor that walketh in his uprightness, than he that is perverse in his ways, though he be rich.

Pro.28.11.bsb: A rich man is wise in his own eyes, but a poor man with discernment sees through him.
Pro.28.11.kjv: The rich man is wise in his own conceit; but the poor that hath understanding searcheth him out.

Pro.28.19.bsb: The one who works his land will have plenty of food, but whoever chases fantasies will have his fill of poverty.
Pro.28.19.kjv: He that tilleth his land shall have plenty of bread: but he that followeth after vain persons shall have poverty enough.

Pro.29.14.bsb: A king who judges the poor with fairness—his throne will be established forever.
Pro.29.14.kjv: The king that faithfully judgeth the poor, his throne shall be established for ever.

Pro.29.7.bsb: The righteous consider the cause of the poor, but the wicked have no regard for such concerns.
Pro.29.7.kjv: The righteous considereth the cause of the poor: but the wicked regardeth not to know it.

Pro.31.9.bsb: Open your mouth, judge righteously, and defend the cause of the poor and needy.
Pro.31.9.kjv: Open thy mouth, judge righteously, and plead the cause of the poor and needy.

Pro.22.7.bsb: The rich rule over the poor, and the borrower is slave to the lender.
Pro.22.7.kjv: The rich ruleth over the poor, and the borrower is servant to the lender.

Pro.22.16.bsb: Oppressing the poor to enrich oneself or giving gifts to the rich will surely lead to poverty.
Pro.22.16.kjv: He that oppresseth the poor to increase his riches, and he that giveth to the rich, shall surely come to want.

Pro.28.3.bsb: A destitute leader who oppresses the poor is like a driving rain that leaves no food.
Pro.28.3.kjv: A poor man that oppresseth the poor is like a sweeping rain which leaveth no food.

Pro.28.15.bsb: Like a roaring lion or a charging bear is a wicked ruler over a helpless people.
Pro.28.15.kjv: As a roaring lion, and a ranging bear; so is a wicked ruler over the poor people.

Pro.2.3.bsb: if you truly call out to insight and lift your voice to understanding,
Pro.2.3.kjv: Yea, if thou criest after knowledge, and liftest up thy voice for understanding;

Pro.2.5.bsb: then you will discern the fear of the LORD and discover the knowledge of God.
Pro.2.5.kjv: Then shalt thou understand the fear of the Lord, and find the knowledge of God.

Pro.15.29.bsb: The LORD is far from the wicked, but He hears the prayer of the righteous.
Pro.15.29.kjv: The Lord is far from the wicked: but he heareth the prayer of the righteous.

Pro.1.23.bsb: If you had repented at my rebuke, then surely I would have poured out my spirit on you; I would have made my words known to you.
Pro.1.23.kjv: Turn you at my reproof: behold, I will pour out my spirit unto you, I will make known my words unto you.

Pro.1.31.bsb: So they will eat the fruit of their own way, and be filled with their own devices.
Pro.1.31.kjv: Therefore shall they eat of the fruit of their own way, and be filled with their own devices.

Pro.1.32.bsb: For the waywardness of the simple will slay them, and the complacency of fools will destroy them.
Pro.1.32.kjv: For the turning away of the simple shall slay them, and the prosperity of fools shall destroy them.

Pro.1.33.bsb: But whoever listens to me will dwell in safety, secure from the fear of evil.”
Pro.1.33.kjv: But whoso hearkeneth unto me shall dwell safely, and shall be quiet from fear of evil.

Pro.9.6.bsb: Leave your folly behind, and you will live; walk in the way of understanding.”
Pro.9.6.kjv: Forsake the foolish, and live; and go in the way of understanding.

Pro.28.1.bsb: The wicked flee when no one pursues, but the righteous are as bold as a lion.
Pro.28.1.kjv: The wicked flee when no man pursueth: but the righteous are bold as a lion.

Pro.2.9.bsb: Then you will discern righteousness and justice and equity—every good path.
Pro.2.9.kjv: Then shalt thou understand righteousness, and judgment, and equity; yea, every good path.

Pro.2.10.bsb: For wisdom will enter your heart, and knowledge will delight your soul.
Pro.2.10.kjv: When wisdom entereth into thine heart, and knowledge is pleasant unto thy soul;

Pro.2.11.bsb: Discretion will watch over you, and understanding will guard you,
Pro.2.11.kjv: Discretion shall preserve thee, understanding shall keep thee:

Pro.2.12.bsb: to deliver you from the way of evil, from the man who speaks perversity,
Pro.2.12.kjv: To deliver thee from the way of the evil man, from the man that speaketh froward things;

Pro.4.18.bsb: The path of the righteous is like the first gleam of dawn, shining brighter and brighter until midday.
Pro.4.18.kjv: But the path of the just is as the shining light, that shineth more and more unto the perfect day.

Pro.13.5.bsb: The righteous hate falsehood, but the wicked bring shame and disgrace.
Pro.13.5.kjv: A righteous man hateth lying: but a wicked man is loathsome, and cometh to shame.

Pro.25.26.bsb: Like a muddied spring or a polluted well is a righteous man who gives way to the wicked.
Pro.25.26.kjv: A righteous man falling down before the wicked is as a troubled fountain, and a corrupt spring.

Pro.21.21.bsb: He who pursues righteousness and loving devotion finds life, righteousness, and honor.
Pro.21.21.kjv: He that followeth after righteousness and mercy findeth life, righteousness, and honour.

Pro.2.4.bsb: if you seek it like silver and search it out like hidden treasure,
Pro.2.4.kjv: If thou seekest her as silver, and searchest for her as for hid treasures;

Pro.8.34.bsb: Blessed is the man who listens to me, watching daily at my doors, waiting at the posts of my doorway.
Pro.8.34.kjv: Blessed is the man that heareth me, watching daily at my gates, waiting at the posts of my doors.

Pro.29.21.bsb: A servant pampered from his youth will bring grief in the end.
Pro.29.21.kjv: He that delicately bringeth up his servant from a child shall have him become his son at the length.

Pro.12.9.bsb: Better to be lightly esteemed yet have a servant, than to be self-important but lack food.
Pro.12.9.kjv: He that is despised, and hath a servant, is better than he that honoureth himself, and lacketh bread.

Pro.13.17.bsb: A wicked messenger falls into trouble, but a faithful envoy brings healing.
Pro.13.17.kjv: A wicked messenger falleth into mischief: but a faithful ambassador is health.

Pro.19.10.bsb: Luxury is unseemly for a fool—how much worse for a slave to rule over princes!
Pro.19.10.kjv: Delight is not seemly for a fool; much less for a servant to have rule over princes.

Pro.25.13.bsb: Like the cold of snow in the time of harvest is a trustworthy messenger to those who send him; he refreshes the soul of his masters.
Pro.25.13.kjv: As the cold of snow in the time of harvest, so is a faithful messenger to them that send him: for he refresheth the soul of his masters.

Pro.26.6.bsb: Like cutting off one’s own feet or drinking violence is the sending of a message by the hand of a fool.
Pro.26.6.kjv: He that sendeth a message by the hand of a fool cutteth off the feet, and drinketh damage.

Pro.27.18.bsb: Whoever tends a fig tree will eat its fruit, and he who looks after his master will be honored.
Pro.27.18.kjv: Whoso keepeth the fig tree shall eat the fruit thereof: so he that waiteth on his master shall be honoured.

Pro.27.27.bsb: You will have plenty of goats’ milk to feed you—food for your household and nourishment for your maidservants.
Pro.27.27.kjv: And thou shalt have goats’ milk enough for thy food, for the food of thy household, and for the maintenance for thy maidens.

Pro.29.19.bsb: A servant cannot be corrected by words alone; though he understands, he will not respond.
Pro.29.19.kjv: A servant will not be corrected by words: for though he understand he will not answer.

Pro.30.10.bsb: Do not slander a servant to his master, or he will curse you, and you will bear the guilt.
